Incremental (partial) growthcleanr run

Source: R/gc_partial_run.R
gc_partial_run.Rd

Re-clean only the subjects whose data changed since a previous cleangrowth run, and reuse the earlier cleaned results for everyone else. This is intended for workflows that repeatedly clean a mostly unchanging dataset – for example a simulation loop that perturbs a subset of subjects and re-cleans – where a full re-run would waste most of its work.

Usage

gc_partial_run(new_data, cached_output, changed_subjids, ...)

Arguments

new_data

A long-format data.frame/data.table of the current data, using growthcleanr's canonical column names (subjid, param, agedays, sex, measurement) plus a per-row id.

cached_output

The data.table returned by a previous cleangrowth() run on the earlier version of this dataset.

changed_subjids

Required. A vector of subjid values whose data changed since cached_output was produced and must be re-cleaned. Any subject present in new_data but not in cached_output (added) is re-cleaned automatically; any subject in cached_output but not in new_data (removed) is dropped. May be length 0 (re-clean only added subjects, if any). Values not present in new_data are ignored.

...

Passed verbatim to the inner cleangrowth call on the changed subset (e.g. checkpoint_dir, checkpoint_size, batch_size, cf_rescue, output switches). Must match the options used to produce cached_output.

Value

A data.table with the same columns as cleangrowth() would return under the same ..., containing every subject in new_data, ordered by id.

Details

gc_partial_run() is a thin wrapper: it slices new_data down to the changed (and any newly added) subjects, hands that subset to a single ordinary cleangrowth() call, and row-binds the freshly cleaned rows to the retained rows of cached_output. All arguments in ... – including checkpoint_dir, checkpoint_size, batch_size, and every output-column switch – are forwarded verbatim to that inner cleangrowth() call, so a large changed subset can still be checkpointed. The cache itself is never passed into cleangrowth(); the merge happens entirely at the output level.

Why the result is correct. After reference-based recentering, growthcleanr cleans each subject independently of every other subject, so cleaning only the changed subjects yields the exact same rows those subjects would receive in a full run. The combined result is therefore identical to cleangrowth(new_data, ...) for a given set of options (see Examples).

Caller responsibilities.

  • ... must specify the same options used to produce cached_output (same cf_rescue, permissiveness, output switches, etc.). If the requested output columns differ from those in cached_output, the function stops rather than silently produce NA-filled rows.

  • id must be present and unique per row in both new_data and cached_output, and must be stable across runs (the same measurement keeps the same id). id is how retained cached rows and freshly cleaned rows are ordered in the output.

  • Input must be long format (one measurement per row). Wide and semi-wide input are not supported by this wrapper.

See also

cleangrowth

Examples

# \donttest{
# Baseline clean of the full dataset
baseline <- cleangrowth(syngrowth)
#> [14:12:10] growthcleanr: cleaning in progress — 2,697 subjects, 77,721 measurements, 1 batch of up to 5,000 subjects
#> ************************************************************
#> growthcleanr cleaning summary  (77,721 measurements)
#>   Weight      : 33,631 included (78.2%), 9,348 excluded (21.8%)
#>   Height      : 26,318 included (75.8%), 8,424 excluded (24.2%)
#>   Set aside   : 0 (0.0%)
#> ************************************************************

# Suppose one subject's data was corrected; re-clean only that subject
changed <- syngrowth$subjid[1]
updated <- gc_partial_run(syngrowth, baseline, changed_subjids = changed)
#> [14:14:08] growthcleanr: cleaning in progress — 1 subjects, 26 measurements, 1 batch of up to 5,000 subjects
#> ************************************************************
#> growthcleanr cleaning summary  (26 measurements)
#>   Weight      : 10 included (71.4%), 4 excluded (28.6%)
#>   Height      : 10 included (83.3%), 2 excluded (16.7%)
#>   Set aside   : 0 (0.0%)
#> ************************************************************

# Identical to a full re-run (same options), for every subject
full <- cleangrowth(syngrowth)
#> [14:14:09] growthcleanr: cleaning in progress — 2,697 subjects, 77,721 measurements, 1 batch of up to 5,000 subjects
#> ************************************************************
#> growthcleanr cleaning summary  (77,721 measurements)
#>   Weight      : 33,631 included (78.2%), 9,348 excluded (21.8%)
#>   Height      : 26,318 included (75.8%), 8,424 excluded (24.2%)
#>   Set aside   : 0 (0.0%)
#> ************************************************************
identical(updated[order(id)]$exclude, full[order(id)]$exclude)
#> [1] TRUE
# }
